_comment: CANONICAL breathing-technique catalogue. Model.js embeds this verbatim as Model.TECHNIQUES; ~/.local/bin/omarchy-breathe embeds the same JSON. test/catalogue.test.sh asserts all three agree. Edit here first, then propagate.

techniques.name: Box
techniques.blurb: Equal inhale, hold, exhale, hold. The steady one — settles a racing head without making you sleepy.

techniques.name: 4-7-8 Relaxing
techniques.blurb: A short inhale, a long hold, and a very long exhale. Weighted hard toward the parasympathetic side.
techniques.use: Falling asleep, winding down, coming off adrenaline.

techniques.name: Coherent
techniques.blurb: Six breaths a minute, no holds. Sits near the resonant frequency where heart-rate variability peaks.
techniques.use: Long calm stretches, HRV training, background breathing while you work.

techniques.name: Physiological Sigh
techniques.blurb: A full inhale, a second sip on top of it, then a long slow release. Reinflates collapsed alveoli and dumps CO2 fast.
techniques.use: Acute stress, the fastest way down from a spike. Two or three is often enough.

techniques.name: Extended Exhale
techniques.blurb: Exhale twice as long as the inhale. The simplest lever on the vagus nerve there is.
techniques.use: General downshift when you want no holds and nothing to count wrong.

techniques.name: Wim Hof
techniques.blurb: Thirty full power breaths, then empty the lungs and hold, then one recovery breath held at the top.
techniques.use: Energy, cold exposure, deliberate stress. Never in water, never driving.
techniques.warning: Sit or lie down. Lightheadedness is expected; blacking out is not. Never do this in or near water.

techniques.name: Bellows
techniques.blurb: Fast, forceful, equal in and out through the nose. Bhastrika — a stimulant, not a sedative.
techniques.use: Waking up, shaking off an afternoon slump.
techniques.warning: Stop if you feel dizzy. Not for pregnancy, uncontrolled hypertension, or on a full stomach.

techniques.name: Triangle
techniques.blurb: Box breathing minus the bottom hold. Keeps a light forward momentum instead of fully parking.
techniques.use: Alert calm — steady but not sleepy.

techniques.name: Vortex
techniques.blurb: A descending run down the Fibonacci sequence — 13, 8, 5, 3, 2, 1 seconds a breath, each one lighter than the last. The shortening pace does the settling; you just follow it down.
techniques.use: Morning practice, clearing a busy head, dropping into a rhythm without counting. Let the short breaths stay light — no need to force them.

techniques.name: Buteyko
techniques.blurb: Deliberately light, reduced breathing with a pause after each exhale. Builds tolerance to CO2 rather than chasing more air.
techniques.use: Over-breathing, mouth breathing, air hunger. Breathe less than feels natural.

techniques.name: Alternate Nostril
techniques.blurb: Nadi Shodhana. Close one nostril, breathe, switch, repeat. One cycle covers both sides.
techniques.use: Balancing, pre-meditation, when box breathing feels too mechanical.

techniques.name: Pursed Lip
techniques.blurb: In through the nose, out slowly through pursed lips as if cooling soup. Keeps the airways open against back-pressure.
techniques.use: Breathlessness, recovery after exertion, tight chest.
